name: FirstSource
desc:
Patient Financial Recovery Specialist | $17-$20/hr | Phone Heavy, Payment Collection & Insurance Verification
Company: FirstSource Healthcare
Industry: Healthcare | Patient Billing & Financial Recovery
What Your Day Will Look Like:
 FirstSource provides outsourced billing and revenue cycle services for hospitals, and this role has you helping patients settle their outstanding balances. You're handling both inbound calls (patients calling with questions) and outbound calls through an automated dialing system, walking people through payment options for what they owe.
Beyond just collecting payments, you're doing real account investigation work: gathering updated insurance information, reviewing "Explanation of Benefits" statements to understand payment discrepancies, and evaluating patients for charity care eligibility when they genuinely can't pay. You're processing credit card payments directly over the phone and navigating multiple patient account and payment systems, all while keeping detailed, accurate notes. This role has real collection and productivity targets built in, so it blends customer service with genuine accountability to hit numbers.

Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: High school diploma or equivalent.
 Required Experience: Not specified by years in posting.
 Preferred Experience: Previous customer service or call center experience. Previous medical billing experience.
 Required Skills:
Effective communication with patients, colleagues, and management, in person or via remote/virtual chat
Self-discipline to stay productive with minimal supervision
Initiative and creativity in fulfilling responsibilities
Strong time management and prioritization across multiple tasks
PC proficiency with typing speed of 30-40 WPM
Strict confidentiality with account information
Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
Someone comfortable having direct conversations about money and payment while staying warm and solution-focused
Participants who can work independently with minimal supervision and stay disciplined without someone checking in constantly
Anyone interested in healthcare billing and revenue cycle work, no prior medical billing experience required, just preferred
People who don't mind real collection and productivity targets as part of daily performance expectations
Not a Good Fit for:
Participants who would struggle with the collections aspect of this role, discussing overdue balances is a core, daily function
Someone who needs more structure and closer supervision to stay on task
Anyone uncomfortable evaluating sensitive financial situations (charity care eligibility) with patients

notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
Application
Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you.
If assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen.
If phone screen passes you can expect the final interview.
 Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3-15 days on average.
4-5 interview questions for this role:
Tell me about a time you had a direct conversation with someone about money owed, and how you handled it professionally.
How do you stay productive and focused when working independently with minimal supervision?
Describe your experience reviewing insurance documentation, like an Explanation of Benefits, to resolve a discrepancy.
How do you approach a conversation with a patient who genuinely cannot afford to pay their balance?
What does maintaining confidentiality look like in your daily work handling sensitive account information?
